tool_schemas.name: get_service_status
tool_schemas.description: Current version per region, health and error rate of a service.

tool_schemas.name: list_deployments
tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: deploy
tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: create_incident
tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy: rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (error rate was 0.18). v2.3.1 was marked unhealthy in production. I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Post-rollback status: healthy, error rate 0.002, all regions on v2.3.0. v2.3.1-rc was unhealthy in staging and was not deployed to production. Follow-up needed: investigate the v2.3.1 failure before re-attempting the release.

trace.final:
checkout-api is rolled back to v2.3.0 in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and is healthy again, with the error rate down from 0.18 to 0.002.

- **Why v2.3.0:** It is the most recent production release marked healthy. v2.3.1 is unhealthy in production. v2.3.1-rc was only deployed to staging, where it was also unhealthy. Because v2.3.0 has a healthy production history, no change-manager approval was needed.
- **Incident:** I opened SEV2 incident INC-0001 for checkout-api. It describes the failure, the rollback, and the post-rollback state, and it paged the on-call engineer. The first request timed out, so I retried with the same idempotency key. That key guarantees only one incident was created.

v2.3.1 needs investigation before it is released again.
